the identification of the most electrophysiologically-active compound in a carrot leaf volatile extract.
the isolation and identification of a sesquisabinene from the leaves of the carrot (Dauc. carota L.) as an active compound against the carrot psylla, T. apicalis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sesquisabinene is a compound that is electrophysiologically and behaviorally active to the carrot leaf feeding psyllid T. apicalis.
sesquisabinene-B is an electrophysiological active compound to the carrot psyllyd, T. apicalis.
sesquisabinene B was identified as an active compound in a carrot leaf volatile extract and that this compound was electrophysiologically confirmed active to carrot psyllid by GC–SSR.
The main takeaway from our work is that

sesquisabinene B, which is a minor component of carrot leaf extract, has a high activity to the carrot psyllyid, and that preparative GC can be used to obtain pure compounds from complex mixtures for further identification.
preparative GC is a useful method to separate and concentrate active compounds from complex mixtures.

sesquisabinene-B is an electrophysiologically and behaviorally active compound for the carrot psyllids and that preparative GC is a valuable tool to isolate and concentrate biologically active compounds in plant extracts.
